result.topic_en: A problem on the law of the sequence of differences of the integer parts of an arithmetic progression A, A+p, A+2p, ..., solved via the continued fraction expansion of p and associated recursive schemes.
result.transcription:
Math 5 Problema. (15) [-40i/46-]

Sunt $A$, $p$ quantitates fractae sive rationales sive surdae: integri proxime minores quam $A$, $A+p$, $A+2p$, $A+3p$ etc. sunt $a, a', a'', a'''$ etc.: Quaeritur lex progressionis $(\Omega)$... $a'-a$, $a''-a'$, $a'''-a''$ etc.

Fundamentum solutionis huius problematis situm est in schematibus sequentibus.

$p = i + r$
$1 = kr + r'$
$r' = k'r' + r''$
$r' = k''r'' + r'''$
etc.
$i, k, k', k''$ integri; $r, r', r''$ etc. posit. et $<$ $1, r, r'$ etc. resp.

$p = i + \cfrac{1}{k + \cfrac{1}{k' + \cfrac{1}{k'' + \text{etc.}}}}$

$m = i$ \quad $n = 1$
$m' = km + 1$ \quad $n' = kn$
$m'' = k'm' + m$ \quad $n'' = k'n' + n$
$m''' = k''m'' + m'$ \quad $n''' = k''n'' + n'$
etc.

$G = i$ continet term. $n$
$G' = (k-1)i, i+1$ \quad $n'$
$G'' = G, k'G'$ \quad $n''$
$G''' = k''G'', G'$ \quad $n'''$
$G^{IV} = G'', k'''G'''$ \quad $n^{IV}$
$G^{V} = k^{IV}G^{IV}, G'''$ \quad $n^{V}$
etc.

Si $A = 0$, aut integer, erit $\Omega = G^{\infty}$

Generaliter fiat
$A = \mathfrak{I} + \mathfrak{R}$
$\mathfrak{R} = \mathfrak{R}K + \mathfrak{R}'$ [?]
$\mathfrak{R}' = r'K' + \mathfrak{R}''$
$\mathfrak{R}'' = r''K'' + \mathfrak{R}'''$
etc.

$KG, \Omega = \Omega' = K'G'\Omega''$
$K''G'', \Omega'' = \Omega''' = K'''G'''\Omega^{IV}$
etc.
Tunc consistet
$\Omega$ e consecutivis $G, G'$
$\Omega'$ \quad $G', G''$
$\Omega''$ \quad $G'', G'''$
$\Omega'''$ \quad $G''', G^{IV}$
etc.

Quodsi dantur $A, p$
hinc eveniri poterunt omnia reliqua nec non $\Omega$ in infinitum
Data autem $\Omega$ in infinitum, invenientur methodo inversa
$p$ et pars fracta ipsius $A$.

Si $\omega$ constat e $g^{2n}$ et $g^{2n\pm1}$ erit $g^{2n}$ tunc tantummodo terminus initialis, quando $g^{2n\pm1}$ is esse nequit, unde facile progressio $\omega$ quousque lubet explicari potest.

methods.what: Continued fraction expansion of p via the Euclidean-type remainder recursion
Recursions for numerators and denominators of the convergents
Recursive construction of blocks G of the difference sequence by concatenation, with block G^{(j)} containing n^{(j)} terms
For integer A the difference sequence is the limit block
General case: expansion of fractional part of A relative to the remainders r, giving recursive decomposition of Ω into consecutive blocks G, G'
Inverse method: recovering p and fractional part of A from Ω
methods.quote:
Data autem $\Omega$ in infinitum, invenientur methodo inversa
$p$ et pars fracta ipsius $A$.

items.english: The law of the progression (Ω) a'−a, a''−a', a'''−a'' etc. is sought.
If A = 0 or an integer, Ω = G^∞.

items.english: If A and p are given, all the rest and also Ω to infinity can be derived from this; but given Ω to infinity, p and the fractional part of A will be found by the inverse method.

items.quote: Si $\omega$ constat e $g^{2n}$ et $g^{2n\pm1}$ erit $g^{2n}$ tunc tantummodo terminus initialis, quando $g^{2n\pm1}$ is esse nequit, unde facile progressio $\omega$ quousque lubet explicari potest.
items.english: If ω consists of g^{2n} and g^{2n±1}, then g^{2n} will be the initial term only when g^{2n±1} cannot be it, whence the progression ω can easily be unfolded as far as one likes.
